prompt: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art sprite concept for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: a single EMBER WISP enemy of the Iron Tide, a small feral fire sprite darting through magma caves. A round molten-gold core like a glowing coal, white-yellow at its heart, with two narrow slanted dark-maroon eye slits giving it a fierce, hungry look, facing left. Around the core flicker ragged flame tongues in stepped bands of orange, red-orange and deep ember red, swept backward to the right as if it is rushing forward, the front edge rounded and compact. Behind it trails a thin crackling tail of three or four separate sparks shrinking into tiny dots. Flames are drawn as hard-edged pixel shapes with a dark outline, not soft glow. Teardrop comet silhouette. Side view facing left, centered with a generous empty margin on a perfectly flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background. Crisp chunky pixel art with a 1-pixel near-black navy outline at the sprite's native pixel scale, flat saturated fills with three-step shading ramps lit from the top-left, bold simple shape that stays readable at small size, no anti-aliasing, no smoke, no scenery, no stars, no cast shadow, no glow bleeding onto the background, no text, no labels.
